faq.1.a: Argus answers while the conversation is going and you need the answer right now, not in a recap an hour later. When the conversation is over, you can still ask its record for a summary, tasks, or an email.
faq.1.q: How is this better than notes after the meeting?
faq.10.a: Yes. Every conversation stays as a session. Open its record: you get the full text, and you can ask for a summary, tasks, an email, or flashcards, then copy the answer or save it as a PDF.
faq.10.q: Can I come back to a conversation later?
faq.11.a: The sound of the windows you pick, your microphone, and the screen or window you pick. Every line is labeled as yours or theirs. You decide what it listens to and watches.
faq.11.q: What does it hear and see?
faq.12.a: With text, code, a formula, a table, or whatever the question needs. It can also read the answer aloud, in a voice you pick. It answers questions from the call and ones you type yourself.
faq.13.a: The Mac version is in beta and isn't signed by Apple yet, so macOS asks you to confirm the first launch. You need a Mac with Apple Silicon (M1 or newer) and macOS 14 or later. Open the downloaded file and drag Argus into Applications. Open Argus and click Done, then open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down, and click Open Anyway next to Argus. Then allow the microphone and screen & system audio recording, and restart Argus after you allow screen recording. If it still won't open, run this in Terminal: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Argus.app
faq.13.q: My Mac says it can't verify the developer. What do I do?
faq.14.a: The Windows version isn't signed yet, so SmartScreen warns you on the first launch. Unpack the downloaded zip first (right-click, then Extract All; don't run Argus from inside the zip), then open Argus.exe. When you see “Windows protected your PC”, click More info, then Run anyway.
faq.14.q: Windows says it protected my PC. What do I do?
faq.2.a: The interface, speech recognition, and answers work in nine languages: Russian, Ukrainian, English, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), German, French, Turkish, and Polish. You can set the answer language explicitly, or leave it on “same as conversation” and it will be detected on its own.
faq.3.a: Yes. Add PDF, Word, and PowerPoint files, text, or photos of pages. Each session has its own materials, and Argus uses them in its answers.
faq.3.q: Can I connect my own documents?
faq.4.a: Every setting in the “Invisibility” section really works, and Argus checks it itself rather than just claiming it. But it's a set of specific technical measures, not an absolute guarantee for every version of Windows and every way of recording.
faq.4.q: So no one will notice me for sure?
faq.5.a: Yes. You sign up with an email and password right in the app, with no email confirmation. A small welcome gift lands on your balance right away so you can try it, and there's nothing else to set up.
faq.6.a: There's no subscription. You top up your balance from $5 and pay only for what you use: speech recognition, answers, and voice replies. Money on your balance doesn't expire. The prices are shown in the app, next to the top-up buttons. To let you try it, we give a small amount when you sign up.
faq.7.a: Argus is a small independent project in active development. The core works and is used every day, but some features may still be unstable.
faq.8.a: Recordings, history, and materials stay on your computer. Audio, and questions with screen frames, are handled by third-party services; our server stores only your account, balance, and usage as numbers, with no text of your questions. Details are in the Privacy Policy.
faq.9.a: Any of them. Argus hears your computer's sound and your microphone and sees the screen, so it doesn't matter where the conversation happens: a video call, a browser, or a lecture. It runs on Windows 10 (version 2004 or newer) and 11; the macOS version (14+, Apple Silicon) is in beta.
faq.9.q: Which programs does it work with?
feat.fast.p: Speech recognition and the answer are tuned for speed. The delay doesn't get in the way of the conversation.
feat.h2: A bit more of what's inside
feat.keys.p: Ask, ask about the screen, start and stop recording, hide the window or the overlay: five shortcuts that work while another program has the focus.
feat.lang.p: The interface, speech recognition, and answers work in nine languages. You can set the answer language explicitly or leave it on “same as conversation.”
feat.mat.p: Add PDF, Word, and PowerPoint files, text, or photos of pages. Each session has its own set, and Argus uses it in its answers, not just what it has heard and seen right now.
feat.n10.p: A hard question? Turn on a slower, more careful answer.
feat.n2.p: From the question to the answer.
feat.n3.p: Add files or photos of pages, and the answers will rely on them.
feat.n4.p: Ask, hide, start, stop. They work over any program.
feat.n6.p: Answers and screen open in their own windows on top of your work, or together in one overlay.
feat.n7.p: Answers copy with their formatting, code has its own copy button, and the record saves as a PDF.
feat.n8.p: On every question, only when you call it by name, or only when you ask.
feat.n9.p: Add a few lines about yourself and pick how it sounds: business, friendly, technical or strict.
final.c1.a: A process is an isolated program with its own memory. A thread runs inside it and shares that memory.
final.c1.q: What's the difference between a process and a thread?
final.c2.a: The inner loop starts at zero, so an item is compared with itself. Start it at i + 1.
final.c2.q: Can you look at why my test is failing?
final.c3.q: How much will 10,000 grow at 8% over three years?
final.c4.a: Maybe. Maria sends the estimate by Monday, so promise an answer then.
final.c4.q: Can we offer single sign-on this quarter?
final.c5.a: Of course. Claro. Let me say it again, slower.
final.h2: Try rgus on your next call.

hero.h1:
Listens and watches with you.
Suggests an answer — right away.
hero.lede: Answers with text, code, a formula, or voice. When the call is over, turns the recording into a summary, tasks, or an email.
how.lede: You choose what it listens to and watches. It answers during the conversation and remembers it afterwards.
how.mem.p: Every conversation is its own session. When it ends, open its record and ask for anything: a summary, tasks, an email. A time in the answer is a link to that line.

price.amt.p: Buttons for $5, $10, $20, and $50, or your own amount: whole dollars, from $5 to $500.
price.cta: Install Argus: $0.30 is on your balance right after you sign up.
price.h1: Pay only for what you use
price.lede: There is no subscription. Top up your balance from $5 and spend it on speech recognition, answers, and voice replies. Money on your balance does not expire.
price.n1: Prices are in US dollars and are also shown in the app next to the top-up buttons. They may change; a new price applies only to what you use after that.
price.n2: Refunds of the unspent part of a top-up are described in the Terms of Use.
price.pay.p: You pay by bank card on a secure payment page; your card details never reach us. Prices are in US dollars. The service is digital: your balance is topped up right after the payment, and the program is downloaded from this site.
price.ref.p: Argus is a digital service: nothing is shipped, and your balance is available right after the payment, so there is nothing to exchange. The unspent part of a top-up can be refunded within 14 days of the payment: write to {email}. The payment system’s fee is deducted. Money already spent and the welcome gift are not refunded. This does not limit your rights under consumer law. Details are in the Terms of Use.
price.s1.h: A gift when you sign up
price.s1.p: Create an account right in the app. $0.30 lands on your balance right away: about 30 minutes of speech recognition or around 150 answers.
price.s2.p: Open “Account” in the app, pick an amount, and press “Pay”. The payment page opens in your browser and your balance tops up by itself.
price.s3.p: “Account” shows your balance, your spending for the last 30 days by day and by service, and your top-up history. When less than $0.50 is left, the app warns you.
price.t.note: An answer with a long context or a screen costs more than a typical one.
price.t.sub: You pay only for what you use. On the right, how far each top-up amount goes.
